selection_gate: All 12 candidate mechanisms were compared against the 258-record pre-generation inventory. Candidates were rejected where their transaction, failure class, evidence or remediation path substantially repeated a prior lesson. Similar broad product families were not treated as duplicates when the underlying mechanism was materially different; rationale is recorded per lesson.

lessons.subject: Exact Data Matching (EDM) for DLP: external data feeds, column-to-type mapping and conjunctive/disjunctive match logic
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: indexed CSV/TXT data records -> EDM template maps columns to built-in data types -> All-fields and Any-fields match groups -> DLP sensor/profile -> firewall policy action
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: refresh external data feed or upload file; parse up to 32 columns; match content in inspected traffic; apply allow/log/block/quarantine action; encrypted protocols require deep inspection and client trust of inspection CA
lessons.failure_class: stale or malformed data feed; invalid column/type mapping; deep-inspection gap; flow-mode versus proxy-mode capability mismatch
lessons.evidence_pattern: external-resource status/refresh; EDM template View Entries; DLP logs showing matched data types; packet/content inspection boundary
lessons.remediation_path: validate feed encoding and column indices; use All/Any logic deliberately; check platform limits and refresh; ensure policy/profile binding and deep inspection; verify current inspection mode
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish exact record match logic from regex/dictionary scanning and determine why a compound identity record does or does not trigger
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: source CSV/feed -> EDM column map -> All/Any match evaluator -> DLP sensor/profile -> policy decision
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No FortiGate EDM/exact-data-match mechanism appears in the 30-day inventory. Prior FortiSASE CASB/DLP lessons use API-based SaaS content controls, not FortiGate indexed record matching.

lessons.subject: Remote GUI access to a managed FortiGate: role-gated proxy path over TCP/8082
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager Remote GUI Access admin-profile capability + Device Manager action + FortiManager HTTP proxy listener + FGFM management tunnel to managed FortiGate + separate FortiGate administrator authentication
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: user authenticates to FortiManager; role permission gates Remote Access; browser opens FortiManager address/port 8082; FortiManager proxies GUI session through management relationship; user authenticates to FortiGate; port can be changed
lessons.failure_class: proxy 502/invalid upstream response; permission missing; FGFM tunnel down; custom admin-sport or expired server certificate; SSL inspection or trusthost blocks
lessons.evidence_pattern: admin profile Remote GUI Access; FGFM TCP/541 state; TCP/8082 capture on workstation/FortiManager/FortiGate; FortiGate HTTPS certificate validity
lessons.remediation_path: enable role permission; confirm FGFM up; allow bidirectional port 8082; bypass deep inspection; validate FortiGate admin-server-cert and trusthost; normalize custom admin-sport where affected
lessons.question_fingerprint: separate permission failure, browser-to-proxy reachability, FGFM control tunnel and FortiGate upstream GUI failure
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: administrator browser -> FortiManager 8082 proxy -> FGFM control relationship -> FortiGate HTTPS GUI
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior lesson covers FortiManager's Remote GUI proxy path or the separate TCP/8082 and FGFM control-plane dependencies.

lessons.subject: Device Manager Up/Down state: OFTP connectivity, last-log freshness and upload-mode thresholds
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: Device Manager status derives from OFTP connectivity where supported and/or last log receive age; separate thresholds for near-real-time and scheduled upload; UI status is a derived health signal rather than a packet-level acknowledgement
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: authorize device/VDOM -> receive OFTP/log traffic -> update Last Log Time and rate -> evaluate mode-specific no-log timer -> render Up/Down and chart; post-reboot UI reconciliation may lag behind actual log receipt
lessons.failure_class: false Down state during post-reboot convergence; genuinely stale logs; OFTP unreachable; scheduled-upload threshold misapplied
lessons.evidence_pattern: FortiGate execute log fortianalyzer test-connectivity/get log fortianalyzer setting status; FortiAnalyzer oftpd 3; diagnose fortilogd lograte; Last Log Time and configured thresholds
lessons.remediation_path: distinguish expected 10-15 minute reboot convergence from >30-minute failure; confirm registered/up and increasing receive counters; inspect registration, port 514, OFTP and fortilogd; adjust only the correct threshold
lessons.question_fingerprint: interpret conflicting device status, connection state, last-log timestamp and receive counters without treating one UI field as proof of end-to-end logging
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: FortiGate log producer -> OFTP/receive pipeline -> timestamp/rate counters -> threshold evaluator -> Device Manager status
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior lesson teaches Device Manager's derived status state machine or the difference between OFTP state, last-log freshness and scheduled-upload thresholds.

lessons.subject: MACsec on FortiSwitch: dynamic CAK, RADIUS-derived key material and MKA secure-channel lifecycle
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: port security-mode macsec + port-level profile + PAE supplicant/authenticator; RADIUS MSK derives CAK; MKA negotiates SAK and secure association; GCM-AES data protection
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: configure profile/cipher/replay window/traffic policy -> bind profile and PAE mode to physical port -> authenticate dynamic CAK -> establish secure channel -> rekey SAK on timer -> count protected traffic
lessons.failure_class: MKA/RADIUS authentication failure; profile mismatch; unsupported cipher/model; control packets dropped under congestion; MACsec overhead causes oversubscription
lessons.evidence_pattern: show switch macsec profile; diagnose switch macsec status <port>; diagnose switch macsec statistics <port>; RADIUS/EAP outcome; interface counters and drops
lessons.remediation_path: verify supported model/cipher; align PAE roles and RADIUS trust; ensure security-mode macsec and port profile; prioritize MKA control traffic; shape for 32-byte MACsec overhead; shut port before changing active profile
lessons.question_fingerprint: differentiate CAK derivation/authentication failure from SAK/secure-channel failure and from congestion-induced session drops
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: RADIUS -> PAE supplicant/authenticator -> MSK/CAK -> MKA -> SAK -> MACsec protected Ethernet link
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: The 30-day inventory contains no MACsec, CAK, MKA or secure-channel lifecycle lesson.

lessons.subject: FortiAP LoRaWAN gateway profiles: Basics Station versus UDP Packet Forwarder, CUPS provisioning and TC/LNS traffic
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: FortiAP supported model dual-roles as Wi-Fi AP and LoRaWAN gateway; lw-profile chooses Basics Station or UDP Packet Forwarder; CUPS supplies configuration/certificates/firmware; TC/LNS carries LoRaWAN data
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: define lw-profile and protocol -> configure CUPS and/or TC endpoint, ports and API keys -> bind profile to WTP profile -> FortiGate pushes profile to AP -> AP registers to CUPS and forwards sensor packets to TC/LNS
lessons.failure_class: unsupported AP model; profile not bound to WTP profile; CUPS registration/authentication failure; TC/LNS endpoint or API key mismatch; configuration push not applied
lessons.evidence_pattern: cw_diag -c lw-config output including EUI, CUPS server/port and TC server/port; profile binding and AP firmware/model support
lessons.remediation_path: verify model support; validate protocol and separate CUPS versus TC settings; check FQDN resolution, TCP reachability and API keys; bind lw-profile to correct WTP profile; verify pushed config on AP
lessons.question_fingerprint: identify whether failure lies in gateway profile binding, CUPS bootstrap/control, or TC/LNS data-plane delivery
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: FortiGate WTP profile -> FortiAP LoRaWAN gateway -> CUPS provisioning/control plane and TC/LNS packet-forwarding plane
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior report covers LoRaWAN, Basics Station, CUPS or LoRaWAN Network Server forwarding. Earlier wireless topics are Wi-Fi association, CAPWAP, roaming and radio behavior.

lessons.subject: Role assignment precedence and inheritance: users, hosts, groups, captive portal and device profiler
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: user/host/device/port entities carry roles; multiple role sources evaluated by rank in Roles view; group assignment, captive portal, user-to-host inheritance and device profiler can update role
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: host/user/device is discovered or registered -> role candidates arise from portal, group, inheritance, profiler or manual assignment -> ordered role list selects first matching role -> role drives policy/access classification
lessons.failure_class: unexpected role due to higher-ranked matching group; role not recalculated after group removal; host inherits user role only under defined conditions; local/global role ranking misunderstanding
lessons.evidence_pattern: Roles view ordering; user and host Properties; group membership; portal role field; device profiler match; role and policy outcome on host record
lessons.remediation_path: inspect every role source and rank; explicitly set portal role where required; understand inherited role propagation; remove/adjust higher-ranked group mappings; manually correct stale host role after group removal
lessons.question_fingerprint: resolve conflicting user, group, portal and profiler role assignments by applying precedence and inheritance rules
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: identity/device sources -> role candidate generation -> ranked precedence list -> effective host role -> access policy
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: Prior NAC lessons cover RADIUS group ingestion, captive portal SAML attributes, 802.1X registration and AV compliance, but not the global role-precedence and inheritance evaluator.

lessons.subject: FortiNAC-F 7.6.3 Secure Boot and file-integrity verification: signed firmware trust and runtime protection
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: cryptographically signed GA firmware verified against Fortinet and external authority signatures; boot-critical files hashed at boot/runtime; unsigned upgrade paths blocked by default after signed build
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: firmware image selected -> signature verification -> trusted boot chain -> boot-critical hashes checked -> runtime file integrity monitoring; air-gapped validation does not require internet
lessons.failure_class: unsigned/interim firmware rejected; modified or missing boot-critical file; untrusted downgrade path; mistaken assumption that online connectivity is required for signature validation
lessons.evidence_pattern: upgrade output 'Verifying the integrity of the firmware image'; signature validation success/failure; runtime integrity event/log; firmware build and boot result
lessons.remediation_path: use signed GA image from trusted distribution; verify provenance and supported upgrade path; use documented prechecked procedure only for controlled interim testing with risk acceptance; plan downgrade with confirmation
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish image signature rejection from post-boot file-integrity violation and determine what a prechecked interim install bypasses
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: signed firmware + trust anchors -> boot verification -> boot-critical file hashes -> runtime integrity enforcement -> audit/reboot decision
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior report covers FortiNAC-F signed firmware, boot-time hash verification or runtime integrity enforcement. Prior N+1/MDM/DHCP lessons are separate mechanisms.

lessons.subject: Certificate private-key lifecycle: delete generated user private key after first download
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: global Certificate Management > Policies > General flag controls deletion of FortiAuthenticator-generated user private key after PKCS#12 Export Key Cert download
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: FAC generates user certificate/private key -> administrator or user exports PKCS#12 from End Entities > Users -> download event triggers deletion when option enabled -> later re-export is no longer possible; server certificate and CA lifecycle remain distinct
lessons.failure_class: operator expects repeatable key export but key was intentionally deleted; insecure key retention when policy disabled; mistaken assumption that deleting certificate also revokes already distributed copies
lessons.evidence_pattern: policy setting state; end-entity certificate status/expiry; Export Key Cert availability; controlled test issuance/download and subsequent export behavior
lessons.remediation_path: decide whether one-time key delivery is required; preserve private key securely at enrollment if re-export is needed; keep deletion enabled where redownload is unnecessary; revoke/reissue rather than attempting to recover deleted private key
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish certificate revocation, private-key deletion from FAC, and endpoint-held PKCS#12 copies
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: FAC CA/key generation -> user certificate store -> PKCS#12 download -> conditional server-side private-key deletion -> endpoint-held key
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior report covers the one-time private-key deletion control. Previous FAC topics cover SAML, FIDO2, OTP push, SCEP/EAP-TLS and REST API operations.

lessons.subject: Single secret to multiple approved target hosts using Multiple Target Address template field
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: secret template uses exclusive Multiple Target Address field instead of Target Address or URL; target stores allowlist of IP/range/CIDR/FQDN/wildcard FQDN; launcher prompts for approved destination
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: create template field -> create target using template -> populate approved destination allowlist -> link secret -> user launches RDP/PuTTY or supported launcher -> destination picker validates requested host against allowlist
lessons.failure_class: template contains mutually exclusive Target Address/URL fields; target destination absent from allowlist; wildcard/CIDR too broad; launcher or version does not support multiple target field
lessons.evidence_pattern: template field type; target allowlist entries; launcher destination prompt/autosuggestions; launch target selected and resolved address
lessons.remediation_path: use FortiPAM 1.9+; remove standard Target Address/URL field; define least-privilege allowlist; verify DNS/IP resolution and supported launcher; test allowed and denied destinations
lessons.question_fingerprint: identify why a shared credential can reach only destinations explicitly permitted by a template-bound target allowlist
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: secret template -> target allowlist -> secret credential -> launcher destination selection -> policy check -> target session
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: Prior FortiPAM reports cover JIT elevation, approval workflow, web launcher and TSO/GSO, not reusable credentials scoped to multiple approved destinations.

lessons.subject: Headless Windows Agent 7.5: local configuration and direct Collector ingestion without Supervisor registration
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: Windows Agent deployment_type=Headless; local exported JSON monitor template; direct Collector endpoint; no Supervisor registration/Agent license; device license and EPS/GB-day consumption
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: create Collector-side htpasswd identity -> install agent with Collector IP/port, org fields and DEPLOYMENT_TYPE=Headless -> export Windows Agent template containing EventLog/user-defined files -> copy as fsm_agent_config.json -> agent sends Windows Security and user-defined events to Collector
lessons.failure_class: agent pointed to Supervisor instead of Collector; Collector not IPv4-only; TLS 1.2 disabled; incorrect password/username; unsupported monitor sources; event license accounting misunderstood
lessons.evidence_pattern: Windows Agent service/logs; Collector httpd/ingest logs; template JSON; device licensing and EPS/GB-day usage; event arrival in FortiSIEM
lessons.remediation_path: use Collector IP/FQDN and port, enable TLS 1.2, provision htpasswd credentials, use only supported EventLog/user-defined sources, place exported template at documented path, verify Collector receipt
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish headless local deployment from registered Supervisor-managed agents and identify Collector-side authentication/configuration boundary
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: locally configured Windows endpoint -> authenticated HTTPS Collector -> FortiSIEM Collector -> Supervisor/Worker analytics
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior inventory entry covers Headless Windows Agent, local JSON template or the direct Collector registration bypass.

lessons.subject: Agentless ZTNA: bookmark portal, proxy SSO and SPA-backed HTTPS private application access
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: browser bookmark portal authenticates proxy user through SSO; FortiSASE Security PoP proxies agentless request through SPA hub to HTTPS private application behind FortiGate
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: enable proxy and proxy SSO -> configure user groups and Private Access security profile -> configure SPA hub -> create private web application and bookmark -> geofence -> user authenticates and opens bookmark; traffic bypasses standard SIA tunnel/proxy flow
lessons.failure_class: proxy SSO/deep inspection prerequisites missing; endpoint agent/proxy user conflicts with agentless bookmark; SPA hub policy blocks PoP source; private DNS access type wrong; application not HTTPS or not behind hub
lessons.evidence_pattern: proxy SSO authentication, bookmark portal access, private app URL/host resolution, SPA BGP route and FortiGate policy logs, security PoP source IP
lessons.remediation_path: verify subscription and prerequisites; use separate agentless session context; configure HTTPS app behind FortiGate; align DNS Access Type with SPA routing design; permit PoP source at hub; configure geofencing and Private Access profile
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish proxy authentication, bookmark authorization, SPA routing and private application reachability in an agentless flow
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: browser -> FortiSASE bookmark/SSO -> Security PoP -> SPA hub FortiGate -> HTTPS private application
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: Prior SASE topics cover agent pre-logon, posture tags, browser isolation, DEM, CASB and regional failover; none covers agentless bookmark-based ZTNA transaction flow.

lessons.subject: Per-packet distribution across aggregate static IPsec tunnels in SD-WAN
lessons.mechanism_fingerprint: multiple static IPsec phase1 interfaces marked aggregate-member -> ipsec-aggregate interface -> aggregate added as SD-WAN member -> per-packet load-balancing across member tunnels
lessons.workflow_fingerprint: build parallel IPsec interfaces over separate WAN underlays at both peers -> enable aggregate-member and compatible crypto/network-device settings -> create matching aggregate interface -> add aggregate to SD-WAN -> route traffic through aggregate and observe distribution
lessons.failure_class: one member tunnel not established; peer member mismatch; aggregate not added to SD-WAN; per-packet reordering/fragmentation/MTU or overhead issues; asymmetric underlay reachability
lessons.evidence_pattern: IPsec SA state for each member; aggregate interface status; SD-WAN member health; per-member packet counters; packet sequence and latency observations
lessons.remediation_path: verify each Phase1 and underlay path independently; align member definitions and proposals; confirm aggregate interface and SD-WAN membership; test MTU and application sensitivity to packet reordering; use documented packet distribution behavior
lessons.question_fingerprint: distinguish per-packet tunnel aggregation from SD-WAN session-based member selection and from BGP graceful shutdown
lessons.diagram_fingerprint: WAN1+WAN2 -> parallel static IPsec members -> ipsec-aggregate -> SD-WAN service -> remote aggregate -> LAN
lessons.uniqueness_rationale: No prior report covers per-packet distribution over an aggregate of static IPsec tunnel interfaces; earlier SD-WAN lessons address BGP tags, graceful shutdown, SLA, ADVPN and underlay probes.

cross_topic_uniqueness_checks.result: Distinct: FortiGate indexed local/external records with column-to-data-type match groups versus FortiSASE API-based SaaS content/tenant controls.
Distinct: ranked role resolution/inheritance across entity types versus external identity/MDM attribute ingestion.
Distinct trust/integrity control versus management-plane HTTP proxy.
Distinct endpoint agent deployment and Collector ingestion versus appliance-to-appliance log aggregation.
Distinct bookmark portal proxy-SSO transaction without endpoint proxy configuration versus browser control or agent-based pre-logon.
Distinct L3 IPsec tunnel packet distribution versus L2 multichassis link aggregation.

result: 12 candidate mechanisms selected; no substantial semantic duplicates identified in the current 30-day exclusion inventory.
